rules.value: Use the master brand name 'Barco' for both the company and its products; no sub-branding or product logos are permitted.
rules.note: Barco uses a master brand approach based on customer impact, not company structure.

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Promote the Barco brand as often as possible; only use division or legal entity names when organizational structure truly matters.

rules.value: In external communication (brochures, ads, newsletters, magazines) refer only to 'Barco' without adding division, market, or location.
rules.note: E.g. 'Barco introduces new LED display.'

rules.value: In address information fields use the legal entity name; reference to divisions/business units/locations only in specific external communications (investor, analyst, press) and must include a qualifying word.
rules.note: Qualifying words: 'division', 'business unit', 'location', or 'facility', e.g. 'President of Barco's Entertainment division.'

rules.value: In internal communications, use Barco as often as possible; division/business unit/location names may be used only with a qualifying word when organizational structure needs highlighting.
rules.note: Same qualifying words required: 'division', 'business unit', 'location', or 'facility'.

rules.value: On company stationery and legally binding documents (invoices, letters, faxes, business cards, email signatures), use the legal entity name in the address field, but use 'Barco' as often as possible in the body content.
rules.note: Applies to legal/stationery materials.

rules.value: Visioneering a bright tomorrow
rules.note: This is Barco's brand mantra used when communicating about Barco generally.

rules.value: Visioneering Healthcare, Visioneering Enterprise, Visioneering Entertainment
rules.note: These are the standard terms used when referring to Barco's markets/segments.

rules.value: Use inspirational 'What if' or 'Imagine' statements when talking about segments.
rules.note: Examples: 'What if meetings could be truly inclusive?', 'Imagine diagnosing patients before they get sick.'

rules.value: Natural, everyday-speech writing style
rules.note: Barco uses a natural writing style based on everyday speech.

rules.value: Fancy oratorical touches, bureaucratic phrases, or explicit commercial wording
rules.note: These are explicitly excluded from the Barco writing style.

rules.value: Write from an outcomes point of view
rules.note: Always find the outcome for the customer that will draw his attention.

rules.value: Warm, open, and personal style
rules.note: Readers should feel personally addressed; company should be perceived as warm and open.

rules.value: Barco / the customer (impersonal third person reference)
rules.note: Avoid referring to the company or reader in the impersonal third person when a first- or second-person alternative is natural.

rules.value: American English is the standard for all communication tools, following Cambridge Dictionary spelling rules.
rules.note: Applies globally across all Barco communications.

rules.value: colour
rules.note: American spelling preferred over British spelling in customer-facing copy.

rules.value: grey
rules.note: American spelling preferred over British spelling in customer-facing copy.

rules.value: visualisation
rules.note: American spelling preferred over British spelling in customer-facing copy.

rules.value: centre
rules.note: American spelling preferred over British spelling in customer-facing copy.

rules.value: programme
rules.note: American spelling preferred over British spelling in customer-facing copy.

rules.value: Prefer active voice over passive voice
rules.note: Active sentences are more concise and dynamic, e.g. 'A buys B' instead of 'B is bought by A.'

rules.value: Jargon and technical terms for general/wide audiences
rules.note: Jargon should only be used for specialist audiences; if used in general texts it must be explained on first use.

rules.value: Use short, frequently used words and simple sentence constructions
rules.note: Important since much of the audience is non-native English speakers.

rules.value: Keep paragraphs as units of thought, not units of length, and avoid long paragraphs
rules.note: Aim for a maximum sentence length of 25 words.

rules.value: Spell out abbreviations in full on first appearance with the abbreviation in brackets, unless the abbreviation is more common than the full form.
rules.note: Acronyms are written in all capitals (e.g. NATO); pronounceable word-abbreviations are written as plain text (e.g. Unicef).

rules.value: Spell out numerals one to ten in words, except for page references and percentages; use figures for numerals 11 and above, decimals, and fractions.
rules.note: Do: 'Two contracts', 'Page 3', '8%', '24 displays'. Don't: '2 contracts', 'Page three', 'Eight percent', 'Twenty-four displays.'

rules.value: Write phone and fax numbers as: +country code, area code, number.
Write dates consistently as day/month/year.
rules.note: Do: '3 June 2004', 'June 3, 2003'. Don't: '3rd June 2003', '3rd of June, 2003.'

rules.value: In running text, place the currency symbol before the figure with no space; abbreviate million as 'm', always spell out billion; if currency symbol omitted, put currency name after the figure.
rules.note: Do: 'â‚¬250 million', 'â‚¬250m', 'â‚¬32 billion', '32 billion euro'. Don't: 'â‚¬ 250million', 'â‚¬250 m', 'â‚¬32 bn', 'euro 32 billion.'

rules.value: Headlines should be active, present tense, and short (preferably no more than two lines).
rules.note: Applies to titles and headlines in brochures and other communication tools.

rules.value: Titles use standard spelling rules with initial capital only for the first word of the title.
rules.note: Example: 'Barco wins $25 million contract for LED installation at Leira stadium.'

rules.value: BARCO (all caps)
rules.note: Barco should always be written in lower case with only the initial letter capitalized.

rules.value: Visioneering a bright tomorrow (lower case with capital V)
rules.note: The brand mantra is consistently written in lower case with a capital V only.

rules.value: Copyright notices should contain the copyright symbol, year of first publication, and owner, e.g. 'Â© 2023, Barco.'
rules.note: Barco is written in lower case with capital B in copyright notices; avoid all-caps.

rules.value: Product names should use one of three naming approaches: fully descriptive name, compound word highlighting USPs, or product code; precede the name with 'Barco' for brand protection.
rules.note: Examples: Barco Canvas, ClickShare, Barco UniSee.

rules.value: Trademarking products other than the Barco name and logo
rules.note: Barco is a branded house; only Barco name/logo should be trademarked, with rare exceptions for crown jewel products, competitive reasons, new market entry, or inherited trademarks from acquisitions (e.g. UniSee, ClickShare, wePresent).

rules.value: Confident and future-facing
rules.note: Blogger observes Barco's marketing comes across as confident and forward-looking (chunk-19).

rules.value: Inspirational, almost sci-fi
rules.note: Uses 'what if' style aspirational questions (e.g., 'what if surgery could happen from anywhere'), giving an inspirational, slightly sci-fi feel (chunk-19).

rules.value: visioneering
rules.note: Barco's own coined term, a mashup of 'vision' + 'engineering', used in their marketing (chunk-19).

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: They refer to themselves simply as 'Barco' rather than using long corporate-speak division names, except in investor-relations documents; reflects a 'one brand' approach (chunk-20).

rules.value: Plain, not flowery
rules.note: Writing style avoids flowery language (chunk-20).

rules.value: Short sentences
rules.note: Sentences tend to be short (chunk-20).

rules.value: Matter-of-fact
rules.note: Overall tone described as matter-of-fact (chunk-20).

rules.value: Not heavily jargon-laden
rules.note: Even in technical content about projectors and LED walls, avoids heavy jargon (chunk-20).

rules.value: inspirational
rules.note: Autumn campaign copy can lean slightly more inspirational, using 'What if' framing and 'Visioneering' language, while still following standard tone-of-voice rules.

rules.value: Barco
rules.note: Use 'Barco' in lower case with a capital B, per the capitalization section of the main guide.

rules.value: BARCO (full caps)
rules.note: Never write the brand name in full caps; use 'Barco' with only the initial letter capitalized.

rules.value: All copy requires sign-off from brand@barco.example before publishing
rules.note: Reminder that all copy still needs approval from brand@barco.example prior to publication.
